rules.title: Supplier liability cap of at least 12 months' fees
rules.description: The supplier's aggregate liability cap must be at least the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
rules.redline: Replace the cap with: 'shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim'.

rules.title: No uncapped customer liability
rules.description: Our liability must never be unlimited; it must be capped at no more than the supplier's cap.
rules.redline: Make the cap mutual: 'Each party's total aggregate liability shall not exceed ...'.

rules.title: Limitation of liability clause present
rules.description: Every supplier agreement must contain a limitation of liability clause.
rules.redline: Insert the standard limitation of liability clause.

rules.title: Customer right to terminate for convenience
rules.description: We must be able to terminate for convenience on no more than 90 days' notice.

any_of: terminate this agreement for any reason

rules.redline: Add: 'Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience on ninety (90) days' written notice.'

rules.title: No auto-renewal with long notice windows
rules.description: Automatic renewal is acceptable only if we can opt out on 30 days' notice or less.
rules.redline: Reduce the non-renewal notice period to thirty (30) days, or require written renewal.

rules.title: Payment terms of at least net 45
rules.description: Invoices must be payable no sooner than 45 days after receipt of a valid invoice.
rules.redline: Change to: 'within forty-five (45) days of receipt of a valid invoice'.

rules.title: Late payment interest no more than 1% per month
rules.description: Late payment interest must not exceed 1% per month.
rules.redline: Cap late payment interest at 1% per month.

rules.title: No unilateral fee increases
rules.description: Fees may only change at renewal and by no more than CPI or 5%, whichever is lower.

patterns: increase the fees at its sole discretion
increase the fees at any time

rules.redline: Replace with: 'Fees may be increased only at renewal, by no more than the lower of CPI or 5%.'

rules.title: Data stays in the UK or EEA
rules.description: Customer and personal data may only be stored or processed in the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area.
rules.redline: Restrict hosting and processing to the United Kingdom and the EEA; transfers elsewhere require prior written consent.

rules.title: No perpetual licence to our data
rules.description: Suppliers may use our data only to provide the services, never under a perpetual or irrevocable licence.
rules.redline: Replace with a limited licence to use Customer Data solely to provide the Services during the Term.

rules.title: Personal data breach notice within 72 hours
rules.description: The processor must notify us of a personal data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.
rules.redline: Change to: 'without undue delay and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware'.

rules.title: Prior notice of new sub-processors
rules.description: The processor must give 30 days' prior notice of new sub-processors with a right to object.
rules.redline: Require thirty (30) days' prior written notice of new sub-processors and a right to object.

rules.title: Audit rights
rules.description: The DPA must give us audit and inspection rights.
rules.redline: Insert the standard audit rights clause.

rules.title: Confidentiality survives at least 3 years
rules.description: Confidentiality obligations must survive for at least 3 years.
rules.redline: Extend survival to three (3) years, and indefinitely for trade secrets.

rules.title: No residuals clause
rules.description: Residuals clauses let the recipient reuse our information from memory and are not accepted.
rules.redline: Delete the residuals clause in full.

rules.title: Return or destruction of information
rules.description: The NDA must require return or destruction of confidential information on request.
rules.redline: Insert the standard return or destruction clause.

rules.title: Approved governing law
rules.description: Governing law must be England and Wales or Ireland.
rules.redline: Change governing law to England and Wales, with exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts.
